description: Deliver a human's external message (for example an iMessage reply). On a Claude or Codex TUI channel this node's input owner holds, the owner takes the input and the answer is delivery=queued reason=accepted; elsewhere, with ADK_BUSY_INJECT=external or all (default off, read once on first use), the input is first offered to the channel's Claude TUI pane when a turn keeps it busy, whoever started that turn (Discord, TUI-direct, background, monitor or adopted). delivery=injected when the transcript records it (turn_id is null unless the busy turn's row names a Discord message), or delivery=unconfirmed with reason inject_unconfirmed and a detail when a paste was attempted but not confirmed (nothing is queued; a busy_inject_unconfirmed alert is recorded). Before the paste the input reserves its place in the channel mailbox, so input sent after it waits behind it. When the pane then refuses the paste, the input takes the front of the queue (delivery=queued, reason handed_back, inject_veto names the refusal); when that queue write fails four times, or its result never comes back, the request fails with queue_refused and detail handback_persistence or handback_unknown, and the input keeps no place in the queue. Otherwise an idle mailbox starts a turn owned by the author (delivery=started), and anything else queues on the channel mailbox with the reason the start was refused (delivery=queued; reason turn_active, background_turn, external_turn_active, turn_activity_unknown or session_transition). external_turn_active means a TUI-direct, adopted or monitor turn holds the channel without the mailbox, or a confirmed turn-mode channel's transcript shows a direct turn running; no start is attempted and the input runs after that turn. turn_activity_unknown means a confirmed turn-mode channel's transcript reads as neither idle nor busy; nothing starts and the queue waits until it reads idle. A queued reply's inject_veto names why the pane did not take it: provider_unsupported, session_unresolved (no Claude TUI pane for the channel, or the host guard keeps it), transition_busy (another session transition or claim handback holds the channel), input_in_flight (an earlier claimed input has not reached the pane), queue_nonempty (earlier input is queued or being dispatched), holder_changed (the holder changed during the lookups), mailbox_unavailable (the channel mailbox did not take the reservation), lock_contended, human_attached, attach_unknown, pane_unavailable, modal, draft, not_busy, transcript_unavailable, load_failed, unpredictable_render (the pane size is unknown or changed before the paste, or Claude's rows for the input cannot be predicted) or invalid_input. inject_veto and detail are omitted when unset. Cancel the active turn in a channel. Default (force=false) requests the preserve path: drain the channel mailbox while leaving the live tmux session and tool subprocesses (cargo, claude CLI, …) alone — the usual meaning of 'queue 정리'. NOTE: this is best-effort, not a hard guarantee. The underlying C-c → SIGKILL → child cleanup can still take the tmux session down as a side effect (e.g. the Claude TUI wrapper exits when `claude` exits). The authoritative side-effect signal is `tmux_killed=true` in the response; treat that flag as the source of truth regardless of `lifecycle_path` (canonical, runtime-fallback, and direct-fallback paths can all report `tmux_killed=true` on the preserve route — `lifecycle_path` only describes which cleanup route ran, not whether tmux survived). force=true tears the tmux session down and SIGKILLs the entire child PID tree; the turn will not complete gracefully. Reserve force=true for explicit recovery (#1196). With the P11 terminate switch on, force=true on this channel's Claude/Codex Herdr execution retires it through the terminate service instead, and the reply adds `termination` with `lifecycle_path: herdr-terminate`. Always inspect `tmux_killed`, `lifecycle_path`, `queue_preserved`, and `inflight_cleared` to learn what actually happened. `dispatch_cancelled` reports the *attempted* dispatch id (the one this cancel-turn correlated to); the underlying postgres dispatch cancel is best-effort and logs warnings on failure rather than aborting the response, so do not treat a non-null `dispatch_cancelled` as proof the dispatch row reached a terminal state — verify via `/api/dispatches/{id}` if certainty is required. `queue_preserved` is nullable: true means measured preservation, false means measured loss, null means unmeasured (formerly true). `queue_disk_present_before/after` are nullable file-existence readings; null means unknown (formerly false). `queue_loss_recorded=true` proves no removal; any unrecorded captured loss is false, and recorded removals or incomplete evidence are null. Force purges with dead-lettered items and preserve calls without a health registry therefore return null. `queued_remaining` uses only depth measured after the last drain/purge attempt; refused hydration (including three purge-closed refusals), unreachable purge, and a purge that finds no global mailbox mirror yield null unless a later guard measured depth. A failed empty save reports the actor post-rollback depth, with `queue_purged=0`; an unreachable purge reports `queue_purged=null`. Clients must accept null without treating it as preservation or absence. See src/server/routes/queue_api.rs::cancel_turn and src/services/queue.rs::QueueService::cancel_turn.

description: List durable campaign DAG checkpoints from canonical PostgreSQL, newest updated first. `live` maps campaign id -> node id -> what the kanban card behind the node's GitHub issue_url is doing now (card_id, card_status, newest dispatch_type/dispatch_status, session_status/session_seen_at of the session holding that dispatch, running, newest auto-queue queue_status); `running` is true only while that session is mid-turn with a fresh heartbeat. description: Body is {idempotency_key,command:{command,...}}. Public commands are start, stop, resume, retry, approve. Start/resume/retry with a valid target return 409 execution_unavailable and create no work. Approve binds node_id, gate, full target (candidate base_sha/head_sha, merge pull_request number/head_sha, deploy main sha), policy_hash and evidence (decision_ref, HTTPS response_ref, response_at) to an already opened gate. Use the pending_gate binding from the current view, including its definition revision. The dashboard copies the stable forum decision ID or slug into decision_ref, the specific approving response HTTPS permalink into response_ref, and its actual RFC 3339 timestamp into response_at. Submit once all three are available. Same gate/evidence approval is idempotent; changed binding or evidence is rejected. Provenance is coordinator_recorded_forum: the coordinator records a checked forum response; the server does not authenticate the forum user. Approvals do not enable execution. Stop accepts mode immediate|finish_stage (202); event advancement does not invalidate its run/definition target. Internal observation/result/completion commands and unknown fields are 400. Conflicts are 409, missing target 404, PostgreSQL absence 503.
